function: Joint learned optimization of the BS precoding matrix and XL-IRS phase shifts (near-field beam focusing) to maximize spectral efficiency (pp. 1-2, 4).
system: Downlink: BS ULA with M=64 antennas, passive reflecting XL-IRS with N=512 elements (UPA, constant modulus), K=4 single-antenna near-field UEs, direct link blocked, 10 GHz (pp. 3-4, 9).
method: Two unsupervised meta-learning algorithms without pre-training: DDAML (dense-connected dilated autoencoder) and CDAML (CNN), trained online per channel sample with Adam on negative SE loss (pp. 4-8).
data_channel: Own simulator: far-field BS-XL-IRS Saleh-Valenzuela/Rician channel and near-field spherical-wave XL-IRS-UE channel, 3GPP TR 38.901 path loss only; 100 independent channel samples (pp. 3-4, 9).
test_conditions: No pre-training: each of 100 channel samples is optimized from scratch; sweeps over power, IRS size, carrier frequency, UEs, NLoS paths, Rician factor, estimation error (pp. 9-13).
baselines: Non-learned: random phase with WMMSE, AO with manifold optimization and WMMSE [13], BFAO [28]. Learned: GMML meta learning [15]; DDAML versus CDAML (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), average CPU execution time, convergence versus epochs, SE retained under channel estimation error (pp. 9-13).
complexity: Big-O of DDAML and CDAML versus AO, BFAO, GMML; CPU time 27.61 s (DDAML) and 13.90 s (CDAML) at N=640 versus 527.93 s for BFAO (pp. 8-10).
q1_support: p. 9: "the path loss model is established according to 3GPP [38]"; the channels are the authors' own Saleh-Valenzuela/Rician multipath and spherical-wave model (pp. 3-4), so only the path loss comes from 3GPP TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 4: "the proposed algorithms do not require pre-training"; each channel sample is optimized from scratch (Algorithm 1, p. 7), so the sweeps of Figs. 6-14 re-run the algorithm and no trained model meets a new condition.
q3_support: p. 9: "Baseline 2 (AO): The traditional optimization algorithm is adopted" and "Baseline 3 (GMML): Meta learning is adopted to solve the SE maximization problem"; p. 10: "Compared to the GMML algorithm, the proposed DDAML and CDAML algorithms achieve 8.09% and 4.46% higher performance at 20dBm"
q4_support: p. 10: "the proposed DDAML and CDAML algorithms achieve convergence in 27.61 seconds and 13.90 seconds, respectively"; p. 8 gives the Big-O complexity of DDAML and CDAML and of AO, BFAO and GMML.
q5_support: p. 9: "compared with benchmark algorithms on Is independent channel samples" generated by the authors' own simulator; the 15 pages contain no code or data link or availability statement (the only URL, p. 15, is an author homepage in the biography).
notes: Title and DOI on page 1 match. Eligibility caution: the networks are trained online on each single channel sample with no pre-training and no train/test split (p. 4, Algorithm 1 p. 7), so the learned component is a per-sample neural-network optimizer; the reviewer may judge it an iterative algorithm (exclude, no_learning), but the paper presents it as unsupervised meta-learning and compares it with the learned GMML [15]. Area 3: joint precoder and XL-IRS phase shifts. q1 is 0 because only the path loss follows 3GPP TR 38.901 (reference [38]). Tables I and II were read from the page image (p. 9).
